headline: Today's 12 km at controlled HR fits the lower easy-run band cleanly, keeping the efficiency signal intact.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
Today's run sits comfortably in the pattern you've built over the last month: an easy-effort 12 km carried at a heart rate that lands in the lower band rather than the one you were running at a block ago. That answers the open question from last week directly — the easy-run efficiency has held so far, though it's worth noting today wasn't a hard session, so the real test of whether it holds under intensity is still ahead.

The bigger picture remains a well-supported build. The recent four-week block is up meaningfully on the prior one, strength volume has roughly tripled over the same window, and the strain-to-tolerance balance reads productive rather than overreached. Nothing here suggests you're overcooked; the load is being absorbed and the durability qualities you care about for a long self-supported crossing are trending the right way.

Sleep is the one wobble worth naming — last night was short following another compressed night, and the recent nights have been uneven. That's supporting context only and shouldn't change what you do, but it's the sort of thing that can quietly accumulate if it runs for a week rather than a couple of days.
watch_items: Whether the run of short nights continues past a couple of days rather than resolving on its own.
Whether easy-run HR stays in the lower band once a genuinely hard session re-enters the schedule — today doesn't test that.
Whether pack-carry running appears in time to adapt to the 6-8kg load before the August crossing.
Whether ascent per run starts trending toward sustained climbing rather than the rolling profiles logged so far.

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 174 km vs 120 km prior block (+45%)
